supporting_observations.claim: The periodic HTTPS activity that matches the alert is attributable in the available endpoint records to ChartMate's cmupdate.exe, connecting through the explicit proxy to update.chartmate-imaging.com. The inventory identifies this updater and its roughly five-minute update checks as approved.

Some ChartMate checks received proxy errors (407 at 13:36 and 504 at 13:45); later checks received 200 responses. These records show repeated attempts and outcomes, not evidence by themselves of malicious activity.

WS-BCARTER-01 made a proxy CONNECT request to drive.google.com at 13:23. The inventory does not approve other file-sharing or cloud-storage services, but this record alone does not establish what content, if any, was accessed or transferred.

Dropbox.exe ran in Ben Carter's user session, and a Cisco AnyConnect VPN UI process ran later in the same session. The records show process execution; they do not establish a Dropbox upload or a VPN connection.
A proxy request to media.akamai.net occurred shortly after Dropbox.exe started, but the provided records do not tie that request to Dropbox.exe; its user agent identifies Firefox.

At 13:46:51, DC-HD-01 recorded Kerberos activity for ben.carter from 10.30.10.24, followed by a successful network logon to WS-BCARTER-01 from that address. The supplied inventory does not identify that address, so its legitimacy cannot be determined from these records.
A failed local logon for ben.carter was recorded shortly afterward. The evidence does not establish whether it was related to the earlier network logon or the user’s activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: Most endpoint network events show connections to the explicit proxy, not direct connections to the ultimate external destination.
Proxy CONNECT records and byte counts do not establish the contents or purpose of transferred data.
The supplied records do not map 10.30.10.24 to an inventoried host or user.
The records show Dropbox and AnyConnect process execution but do not establish file uploads, a VPN session, or the authorization status of their installation.
The available evidence does not include relevant file-access, cloud-service audit, or complete activity records for the source at 10.30.10.24.
claims_not_established: Whether any data was uploaded to Google Drive, Dropbox, or another external service.
Whether the 10.30.10.24 logon was authorized or represents access from an unapproved device.
Whether Cisco AnyConnect was used to establish a VPN connection.
Whether any of the observed activity was performed by Ben Carter, another person using his account, or an automated process.
Whether the non-ChartMate activity is malicious, despite being inconsistent with the supplied service inventory.
additional_evidence_needed: Identify the device and owner assigned to 10.30.10.24 and review its authentication and endpoint records around 13:46 UTC.
Review proxy or cloud-service audit logs for Google Drive and Dropbox activity, including upload/download direction, filenames, and account identity.
Check endpoint inventory and software-management records to determine whether Dropbox and Cisco AnyConnect were installed or authorized.
Review endpoint file-access, browser, and process-network telemetry around the observed cloud-service and logon activity.
Confirm whether any VPN connection was established and whether its use was authorized.
